subject: Customer storage escrow eligibility & technical remote-wipe evidence
messages:
From: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@crescenthealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: security_ops@crescenthealth.com
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment — escrow eligibility and remote-wipe evidence

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week. Crescent is evaluating Redwood Private for our clinical inference pipeline. Two quick questions from security & procurement before we move into a technical POC: 

1) For Private/VPC deployments where storage is customer-controlled, do you offer a storage-escrow or evidence-of-delete package we can rely on in the event of contract termination? We need to understand how the tenant data is handed back or destroyed (and how you prove it).

2) When a tenant is decommissioned, can you provide a timeline for remote wipe and an attestation artifact (hash/time-stamped log, signed by Redwood) that we can store for audit? Our auditors ask for a verifiable chain-of-action.

Could you outline the minimal deliverables (documents/logs/attestations) Crescent would receive and typical turnaround for a region-locked, US-only deployment? We’re targeting a decision by end of May.

Best,
Emma Lopez
Director, Cloud Security
Crescent Health

Attachments: none

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@crescenthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — escrow eligibility and remote-wipe evidence

Emma — thanks, and great questions. Summary below; I’ll loop Legal and Product for the contractual and ops artifacts. Short version: yes, we have a customer-controlled storage model for Private where the tenant store remains in your VPC or a customer-dedicated bucket. We support a documented handback and multiple attestation options.

What we can deliver (minimal package):
- A secure export bundle (encrypted tar) of tenant objects on request, with SHA-256 checksums.
- Time-stamped deletion logs from the host agents (with sequence numbers) showing the wipe operations and per-object tombstone entries.
- Cryptographic attestation: a signed statement (PDF) that references the SHA-256 fingerprints of the exported bundle and the deletion log, signed by Redwood’s Signing Key (KMS-backed).
- Optional on-demand KMS-wrapped key destruction report when we hold any keys on behalf of the tenant.

Typical timeline (US region, hosted in your VPC or customer-dedicated storage):
- Data export and verification: 24–48 business hours (depends on dataset size).
- Scheduled remote wipe (agent-driven): completes within 4–24 hours after confirmation; long tail depends on replication and retention window in the customer store (we do not force-delete resources owned by the customer without explicit authorization).
- Attestation artifact generation: within 24 hours after wipe completion.

I’ve attached a short operational playbook that describes the agent-level wipe and evidence package. Proposed next step: 30-minute call with our Security/Platform ops to walk through the audit artifacts and agree on SLAs (I’m available Thu/Fri).

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Head of Customer Solutions (Redwood Inference)
Phone: +1 415-555-0198

Attachments:
- redwood_data_wipe_playbook.pdf (stub: operational steps + log format)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@crescenthealth.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — escrow eligibility and remote-wipe evidence

Emma / Dylan — marking this for Legal and Contracts input. Quick notes on the commercial side: 

1) Escrow / evidence-of-delete: We can add a Schedule to the Master Services Agreement that spells out deliverables (export bundle, signed attestation, deletion logs) and the timing. I’ve drafted a short clause for your procurement team (attached).
2) Data ownership and keys: If Crescent wants complete control, we recommend customer-managed KMS keys and a limited Redwood access profile. That removes the need for key destruction reports from our side and simplifies attestation language.
3) Fees & SLA: Standard one-off fee for a handback + attestation (covers operational hours and keying) — I’ve included a redline for a typical fee band. If you prefer an annual escrow/validation plan we can price that as part of the deal.

I’ve attached a draft (escrow_terms_draft.docx) for review; Dylan — let me know if Product/legal should expand any technical detail.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- escrow_terms_draft.docx (stub: proposed contract language, fee table)

From: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@crescenthealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: security_ops@crescenthealth.com
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment — escrow eligibility and remote-wipe evidence

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple follow-ups from Security: 
- We will take customer-managed KMS as the default. Please confirm: with CMK in our account, Redwood will never be able to decrypt the exported bundle without an explicit key grant? We need that in writing for our auditors.
- For the attestation, would Redwood be able to produce a signed PDF that includes a timestamp and the SHA-256 fingerprints? Is the signature backed by an HSM?
- Can we get an example deletion log (redacted) and the playbook pointer so engineers can validate format ahead of the POC?

Procurement side: we’ll review the escrow_terms_draft and circle back with redlines. If you can also include a one-page summary that calls out "What Crescent receives at offboarding" (export, checksums, signed attestation, timeline) that will speed internal sign-off.

If you can confirm the CMK behavior and the HSM-backed signature, we’ll lock in the POC start next week.

Best,
Emma

On a separate note, security_ops@crescenthealth.com asked whether Redwood provides a persistent reference ID for each wipe action (so we can reference it from our ticketing system). If you have a recommended format we’ll plug it into our change control process.
